brief: brief-js168-second-viewer.md (JS-168 criterion 5) and the JS-167/JS-168 triage
tradeoff: Who gives way when a second viewer arrives while helpers a first viewer needs hold every worker
serves: PRODUCT.md goal 1: 'Playback never surprises a viewer.' 'every failure is reported with its reason, never silent'. 'Signing in is easy and safe.' 'Failures are invisible.'
entry: D-046's default stands as the rule: a helper of a watched job its own worker does not hold at 1.2 times real time alone is that play's own, and a newcomer whose job fits only by stopping it is refused within seconds with its own reason, whatever it costs; a viewer joining a running re-encode is not a newcomer; no helper is stopped or held back for a play that is not admitted (takes BL-014 and JS-168's gate finding). JS-161 criterion 11 is rewritten so, with a short locked check and the jellyfin-web runs as a recorded measurement; criterion 1 gains the ledgers, the unfittable queued job and BL-008; JS-164 counts the helper-held refusal as its own reason; docs/running.md's transcodeHelpers paragraph and DOMAINS.md invariant 58 change with it. Given up: on a cluster one shared film fills, a second viewer is refused where today they would start, a 1080p one included, by the second viewer. Rejected: B, C and E (the viewer already watching fell from 1.00x to 0.68-0.82x with 44 to 54 freezes in 5 minutes and no reason, 6 runs of 6, and the newcomer started no sooner); D (a picture loss D-044 rejected). Triage: JS-171 at 18 (a test process's port and the seek checks' zero margin, fixed as checks by making less film, never CI capacity or a longer bound), JS-172 at 19 (the unknown-name store has a ceiling no flood raises: never rising flood over flood, over the bound by no more than the sign-ins in flight; a build that meets it has its check and docs/access.md amended to say so, citing this decision, and one that does not is fixed; exactness at rest is a check choice), JS-173 at 20 (a viewer is never refused for the cores of a job just given up; forced first, verdict by D-042); all three build beside JS-161 and hold neither it nor JS-041 and JS-157. The Postgres coordinator measurement joins BL-036; BL-001 and BL-006 close on JS-168 merging; a new backlog item holds a cheap play beside the helper. Unverified when decided: the second-viewer figures are not in docs/transcoding.md on any ref read, and must be before JS-161's Spec; the measured build carried a timeout since removed; whether a helper beside a 0.8-core job keeps the first viewer at real time; the lead's reading of the flood overshoot, and where the 116 rows over 200,000 were. Data that reopens it: the dogfood's count of helper-held refusals against the stalls prevented; a measurement of both viewers within JS-168's bound with the cheap play admitted; a flood whose excess accumulates.
